what: What did each Lunenburg town employee earn in 1964?
why: `report-gross-wages` holds per-employee earnings from the 1995-2010 reports and FY2011-FY2025. The 1964 annual town report prints no wage list: the whole text (12,802 lines) was searched for wage, payroll, gross and salary and found only aggregates (the accountant's `Wages` lines in the schedule p26-37, `Payroll Savings` p20), the Personnel Study Committee's aim to provide wage scales (p10 text) and the school personnel pages (p111-117), which name staff, subject and year appointed and print no pay (sources/data/report-tables/1964/). — closes: the Town's calendar-1964 payroll register (W-2 totals by employee) from the Treasurer's office.

what: What were the town's non-union salary grades and step rates in 1964?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1964 report records only the cost of a `Wage Classification Plan` ($635.00, p17 and p35) and the Personnel Study Committee, not the schedule; searched for classification, salary schedule, grade and step (sources/data/report-tables/1964/). — closes: the Personnel Board's Classification and Salary Schedule adopted for 1964.

what: What did each special revenue fund take in, spend and carry forward in 1964, town-wide?
why: `special-revenue-funds` holds forward, receipts, disbursements and balance by fund from the 2010 report. In 1964 the statement of receipts and payments and the accountant's schedule (p26-37) carry individual accounts (`School Lunch Program` Chapter 417, athletic, adult education, federal grants) but no fund-by-fund statement of receipts, disbursements and balance; searched special revenue, revolving, school lunch and grants (sources/data/report-tables/1964/). — closes: the Town Accountant's calendar-1964 fund ledger.

what: What was appropriated, spent and carried forward on each capital project in 1964, as a fund?
why: `capital-project-funds` holds a fund schedule in the 2010 report. 1964 prints capital articles inside the voted special articles (p64) and the accountant's schedule (unexpended balances carried to 1965, p16-17), not as a capital fund; searched capital, article and construction (sources/data/report-tables/1964/). — closes: the Town Accountant's calendar-1964 capital articles ledger.

what: What was Lunenburg's assessed valuation by property class, its levy, overlay and new growth for 1964?
why: `report-valuation` holds valuation by class and levy history from later reports. 1964 prints the total assessed valuation ($11,483,340 with the real and personal split) and the tax rate ($82.00) as text (p4), the Assessors' narrative of how a tax rate is formed (p7), and the `Overlay Deficit - 1964 levy` on the balance sheet (p16); no valuation by class table, levy or new growth. Searched valuation, tax rate, overlay, levy and recapitulation (pages 4, 7, 8, 16, 17, 37, 53, 63, 93, 103, 121) (sources/data/report-tables/1964/). — closes: the Assessors' 1964 tax rate recapitulation (the Tax Recap sheet filed with the State).

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 1964, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's activity from later reports. 1964 prints the Sealer's narrative (p46, about the State-owned standards) and sealing fees received ($96.80, p20 receipts), with no count or fee by device type. Searched sealer, weights and measures, sealing (pages 5, 20, 22, 28, 46, 63, 122) (sources/data/report-tables/1964/). — closes: the Inspector of Weights and Measures' 1964 test and fee record.

what: Where did the Town's other receipts and payments come from, as a share, in the 1964 `Where Did Your 1964 Tax Dollar Go?` chart?
why: p14 prints a pie of the tax dollar by service in cents (schools 73.2 cents, and slices a-f) and p15 a receipts and payments analysis; Textract read the large slices as page lines only (p14 has no table cells, p15 only the small slices a-i), so the large slices are not in `report-expenditure-shares` as cells. Searched pages 13-15 lines and cells (sources/data/report-tables/1964/). — closes: a readable copy of the p14-15 charts, or the Treasurer's chart workpaper.
